moved.sentence: Put build settings in `.xcconfig` files, not in the project editor's Build Settings tab.

judged.note: Putting build settings in .xcconfig files rather than the editor's Build Settings tab is kept at SHOULD, with the one-line-diff reason as a sub-point.

moved.sentence: Keep one shared file for settings common to every target and one per configuration or target for the differences.

judged.note: One shared xcconfig for common settings and one per configuration or target for the differences is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Add only the settings you want to change.

judged.note: Adding only the settings you want to change is kept at SHOULD in the same rule.

moved.sentence: Leave the target-level Build Settings tab empty for any setting an xcconfig already owns, or the target value silently wins.

judged.note: Leaving the target-level Build Settings tab empty for settings an xcconfig owns, with the target-value-silently-wins reason, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Create the file with "Configuration Settings File" and deselect all targets so Xcode does not embed it in the bundle.

judged.note: Creating the file with Configuration Settings File and deselecting all targets, with the not-embedded-in-bundle reason, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Look up each setting name in the build settings reference before you use it.

judged.note: Looking up each setting name in the build settings reference before use is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Do not guess a name; an unknown setting is ignored without an error.

judged.note: Not guessing a setting name is kept at SHOULD NOT, with the ignored-without-error reason.

moved.sentence: Add one only for a capability the app uses, and review every added key as a security change.

judged.note: Adding an entitlement only for a capability the app uses and reviewing every added key as a security change are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Keep one `.entitlements` file per target and configuration need (for example a sandboxed macOS app and its helper), referenced through the `CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS` setting.

judged.note: One .entitlements file per target and configuration need, with the sandboxed-app-and-helper example and the CODE_SIGN_ENTITLEMENTS reference, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Never copy an entitlements file from another app wholesale.

judged.note: 'Never copy an entitlements file wholesale' is kept as a MUST NOT, with the leftover-key reason as a sub-point.

moved.sentence: Keep the Info.plist small.

judged.note: Keeping the Info.plist small is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Prefer build-setting substitution (`$(PRODUCT_NAME)`, `$(MARKETING_VERSION)`) over literals, so a version or name is set once in the xcconfig.

judged.note: Preferring build-setting substitution over literals, with both examples and the set-once-in-the-xcconfig reason, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Remove keys for features the app no longer has.

judged.note: Removing Info.plist keys for features the app no longer has is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Where the repository already uses XcodeGen (a `project.yml` spec), treat the spec as the source and the generated `.xcodeproj` as an output: regenerate it, do not hand-edit it, and either ignore it in version control or verify in CI that it matches the spec.

judged.note: The whole XcodeGen instruction, including its already-uses condition, regenerate, no hand-edit, and ignore-or-verify-in-CI, is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: XcodeGen's spec points targets at xcconfig files through its `configFiles` option and at settings through its `settings` key; keep real values in the xcconfig and use the spec for structure.

judged.note: The configFiles/settings explanation and keeping real values in the xcconfig with the spec for structure are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Do not introduce a generator into a repository that has none as part of an unrelated change.

judged.note: Not introducing a generator into a repository without one as part of an unrelated change is kept at SHOULD NOT.

moved.sentence: Put the team ID and signing style in the xcconfig.

judged.note: Putting the team ID and signing style in the xcconfig is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Use automatic signing for local development and an explicit, documented identity for release builds.

judged.note: Automatic signing for local development and an explicit, documented identity for release builds are kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Never check in a certificate, a private key or a provisioning profile.

judged.note: 'Never check in a certificate, private key or provisioning profile' is kept as a MUST NOT, with the CI-secret-store sub-point.

moved.sentence: One scheme per thing a person builds, runs or tests.

judged.note: One scheme per thing a person builds, runs or tests is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Delete schemes that no longer build.

judged.note: Deleting schemes that no longer build is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Name targets and schemes after what they produce.

judged.note: Naming targets and schemes after what they produce is kept at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Do not leave `Untitled`, a copied target's `copy` suffix or a stale product name.

judged.note: Not leaving Untitled, a copy suffix or a stale product name is kept at SHOULD NOT in the same rule.

moved.sentence: Keep test targets separate from app targets, and set each target's deployment target explicitly in the xcconfig, not by default.

judged.note: Keeping test targets separate and setting each deployment target explicitly in the xcconfig, not by default, are kept at SHOULD in two rules.

moved.sentence: Review project-file changes against Xcode project hygiene ([adc.guideline.implementing.code-quality.xcode-project-hygiene](cookbook:187a80eb-e2e5-4a6c-8d14-aa591840abe6)).

judged.note: The look-for part keeps the instruction to review project-file changes against this guideline; the self-link becomes 'the rules above', this artifact's own rules part, and the read-order sentence that followed is kept verbatim.
